findings.detail: Covers reads as if Groen only praises Lamartine. In fact Lamartine is his example of the man led astray. 300-302: 'in de beginselen, gevoelens, en verwachtingen van den begaafden auteur, opmerk wat reeds door menig schitterend voorbeeld getoond werd'. 307-331: such a man 'de Rede voor onfeilbaren maatstaf houde der openbaringen Gods' and praises the Revolution 'als van een volkaan voorzeker, maar die onvergankelijke waarheden uitslingert' (footnotes 312-314, 339-341 quote Lamartine on reason and the 'volcan de vérités'). Footnote 341-348 turns Lamartine's 'vieux parti de la routine et du préjugé' back on him. Da Costa's verse 376-383 ('Van Robespierres leer in Lamartines taal') is not mentioned.
findings.fix: Add: 'Groen also shows Lamartine as an example of this. Lamartine treats reason as the judge of revelation and praises the Revolution as a volcano of truths. Groen quotes him, and da Costa's poem against him.'

findings.detail: ocr_notes say footnote 276-282 'belongs to the previous part' (its mark is at 260 'gezien wordt ')'), yet quoted_authors lists Louis Blanc 276-282 and names lists 'Montagne@276' for this part.
findings.fix: Either drop Louis Blanc 276-282 and Montagne from this part, or remove the ocr_notes claim; be consistent.

findings.detail: 'persons subject to a ruinous teaching' is stiff for B2 (Dutch 294-295 'ondergeschiktheid der personen aan den invloed eener heillooze leer').
findings.fix: 'how persons are ruled by a harmful doctrine'

findings.detail: 'The first half is negative' — 951 says 'Het eerste gedeelte van mijn betoog is negatief' (first part, not half).
findings.fix: 'The first part of his argument is negative'

findings.detail: The thesis stated at 948-949 ('Het revolutie-tijdperk ... is de vrucht der revolutie-begrippen') is not in covers.
findings.fix: Open with: 'He states his thesis: the age of revolution is the fruit of revolutionary ideas.'

findings.detail: Footnotes 1013-1015 (marks at 986 and 1007, incl. the Guizot attribution) fall in the next part, while footnote 966-974 belonging to the previous part is listed here (Archives de la Maison d'Orange-Nassau in names and quoted_authors). Disclosed in ocr_notes, but names/QA carry previous-part material.
findings.fix: List Archives under the previous part; note Guizot attribution at 1015.

findings.detail: Sentence of 27 words; and 'he names Baco, Huig de Groot and Leibnitz' is ambiguous — they are named as men who did NOT honour such ideas (1362-1367 'Noch Baco ... noch Huig de Groot ... noch Leibnitz, die ... met ontzetting de voorteekenen eener naderende omwenteling zag').
findings.fix: 'First, apart from Descartes and some English scholars, hardly any great scholar honoured such ideas. Not Baco, not Huig de Groot, and not Leibnitz, who saw in them with horror the signs of a coming revolution.'

findings.detail: Grote, History of Greece, Protagoras (1344-1346) come from a footnote that ocr_notes assign to the previous part.
findings.fix: Move these names to the previous part.

findings.detail: The three-head plan at 2172-2173 ('de misvorming, den aard, en de gevolgen') is not mentioned; this part covers only the first head (2178 'De misvorming').
findings.fix: Add: 'He will treat the doctrine under three heads: its caricature, its nature and its effects. This part gives the caricature.'

findings.detail: Tocqueville / L'ancien régime / Engeland (2180-2185) are from a footnote that ocr_notes say belongs to line 2156 of the previous part, but are listed here in names and quoted_authors.
findings.fix: Move to the previous part.

findings.detail: Covers never says the subject is the union of Church and State; the opponents' claim that abuses lie 'in den aard der vereeniging' (2688-2696) and Groen's conclusion 'mogelijkheid is geen noodzakelijkheid der misbruiken' (2730-2731) are only in the label.
findings.fix: Add: 'Opponents say a Church joined to the State can never be free in matters of faith. Groen answers that abuses are possible, not necessary.'

findings.detail: quoted_authors gives Vinet 2702-2705, a footnote whose mark is at 2672 in the previous part (ocr_notes say so).
findings.fix: Move that entry to the previous part.

findings.detail: 2880-2884: these truths are elementary, our age needs elementary teaching, and modern philosophy 'het alfabet der wetenschap verleert'. Also the long footnote continuation 2851-2861 (unbelief becomes state religion; Vinet, Palmer, Stahl) is not mentioned.
findings.fix: Add: 'He calls these truths elementary and says modern philosophy has unlearned them. A long note argues that, without a Christian Church, unbelief becomes the religion of the state.'

findings.detail: 26-word sentence on von Gentz.
findings.fix: 'He cites von Gentz. Gentz finds views on the source of law in the ancient republics and in Cicero. Christian nations now seem to be losing them.'

findings.detail: 'the decay of constitutional law helped the revolutionary principle to rise' is stronger than 4722-4723 'De opkomst van het revolutie-beginsel is met de verbastering van het Staatsregt in verband'.
findings.fix: 'the rise of the revolutionary principle is bound up with the decay of constitutional law.'

findings.detail: 'A theoretical law' is unclear for 4750-4751 'een theoretisch staatsregt'.
findings.fix: 'A theory of state law'

findings.detail: Groen's own stand is omitted: 6718-6724 'Ik ben voorstander van formulieren ... heb ik onder het ... protest ... mijne naamteekening gevoegd', and footnote 6731-6742 on his protest to the Synod and what he has urged 'van 1837 tot heden (1867)'.
findings.fix: Add: 'He says he signed his friends' protest to the Synod, and a note sets out what he has defended since 1837.'

findings.detail: The turn ('Aanklagt tegen de Roomschen is geen vrijspraak der Protestanten') begins mid-line in 6680, so 6680 belongs to the part in part. Disclosed in ocr_notes.
findings.fix: Start at 6680, or keep as is with the note.

findings.detail: Groen's point that hatred of the gospel marks the Revolution 'geenszins wanneer zij tot buitensporigheid overslaat ... integendeel, wanneer zij, gebleven in haar spoor, het doel ... bereikt' (7658-7674) is lost. The long note 7680-7717 (atheism becomes pantheism and a religion of humanity; Renan, Vinet, Stahl) is not mentioned.
findings.fix: 'He calls hatred of the gospel the mark of the Revolution, not when it goes to excess but when it reaches its own goal. A long note says unbelief turns into a religion of humanity, with its own state religion.'

findings.detail: 'Grondwetherz. en Eensgezindheid@7625' is in the tail of a footnote that ocr_notes say starts in the previous part (7585).
findings.fix: Note it as continuation of the previous part's footnote.

findings.detail: 'Groen says that among free and equal people only a voluntary agreement can form a state, so the social contract is its only origin' gives the revolutionary position as Groen's own. The Dutch makes it conditional on the revolutionary premise and calls it the error: 7922-7923 'naar het revolutionair beginsel'; 7927-7929 'Ligt het revolutionair begrip van vrijheid en gelijkheid ten grondslage van uw gebouw, zoo moet gezag en regt conventioneel zijn'; 7936-7938 'Wij vinden hier de dwaling terug, waarin de verbastering der politieke wetenschap voornamelijk bestaan heeft'.
findings.fix: 'Groen shows how the revolutionary principle forms a state. If people are free and equal in its sense, only a voluntary agreement can join them, so the social contract is the only origin. He calls this the main error of corrupted political science.'

findings.detail: 'De la Mennais@7933' is the attribution footnote of the previous part's quotation (7880-7916).
findings.fix: Note it as belonging to the previous part's quotation.

findings.detail: 'men who served every regime were often faithful to one theory' overstates. Groen grants the indignation is often just ('in menig geval is uwe verontwaardiging billijk', 10466) and says only 'nu en dan voorzeker' (10457-10458) were such men true to a theory.
findings.fix: 'some men who served every regime were, now and then, faithful to one theory through its changes.'

findings.detail: Groen does not vouch for Talleyrand: 10504-10505 'Ik laat daar of de verontschuldiging op den sluwen egoïst ... toepasselijk is'. Also de la Mennais's portrait of the 'race d'êtres pervers' (10421-10432), which Groen says is not of general use, is not mentioned.
findings.fix: 'He quotes Talleyrand's defence of himself, without saying it fits that cunning egoist, to show how widely this view worked.'

findings.detail: The long note 11543-11578 takes St. Marc-Girardin as the example of the claim and answers it from the Mirabeau-La Marck correspondence; covers does not mention it, so a user looking for Mirabeau would miss it. Also 11588 says the accidents were 'grootendeels' (largely) results of the doctrine.
findings.fix: 'the accidents were largely results of the doctrine ... A long note takes St. Marc-Girardin's essay on Mirabeau as the example and answers it.'

findings.detail: The French passage 12341-12353 (deputies usurped the people's rights 'sans droit et sans mandat') is not in quoted_authors; its source at 12372 is garbled. Groen's reply 12353-12354 'Dit is waar; namelijk wanneer men de veranderde denkwijs voorbijziet' is flattened into plain agreement.
findings.fix: Add quoted_authors entry {'author':'unreadable source (12372)','lang':'fra','lines':[12341,12353]}; covers: 'He grants it was a breach of mandate, judged by the old law, but by the new ideas it was right and fitting.'

findings.detail: quoted_authors Burke 12617-12657 spans the anonymous French passage 12629-12664; Burke's text is 12617-12620 and 12655-12657 only.
29-word sentence listing the three means.
findings.fix: 'He names three. The Revolution organised an all-powerful central authority. It shut out those who thought differently. And it set itself free of its own laws when they stood in its way.'

findings.detail: Von Sybel and Nationale Vergadering (12837-12845) are from a footnote that ocr_notes assign to the previous part, yet are listed in names and quoted_authors here.
findings.fix: Move to the previous part.

findings.detail: The argument the label names begins earlier, at 13002-13003 ('Er was gelijkheid van beginsels; was er in de handelingen verschil? ... Er was gestadige opklimming'), and footnote 13013-13017 belongs to it; the part starts mid-argument at Necker.
findings.fix: Start the part at 13002 (or 13001 '—  Er was gelijkheid'), or relabel as 'Necker and Chateaubriand on the rising violence'.

findings.detail: Roland in 1792 calling the September killings 'excès, effervescence, agitation' (13029-13032) is not mentioned though Roland is in names.
findings.fix: Add: 'He also blames Roland for softening the September killings of 1792.'

findings.detail: 26-word sentence on the moderates.
findings.fix: 'Under point 1 he says the moderates who took power after the Terror kept the revolutionary theory. They drew their middle line by mere choice.'

findings.detail: ocr_notes 'read the end date from the print' for '1794—4845' is no reading; the heading year is unresolved.
findings.fix: 'End year prints 4845; first digit is an OCR fault (1845 likely, not certain).'

findings.detail: 'Rijk der Nederlanden@17108' first appears at 17086 ('rijk der Nederhuiden'); 'Holland@17112' first appears at 17098 ('van Belgïe tot Holland').
findings.fix: Rijk der Nederlanden@17086; Holland@17098.

findings.detail: The north's liberal caution out of self-defence against the Belgians (17105-17128), and Dutch approval of Charles X's fall and of Louis-Philippe (17132-17140), are not in covers.
findings.fix: Add: 'The North, he says, turned cautious only in self-defence against the Belgians. The Dutch also applauded Louis-Philippe and copied his politics.'

overall: The guide is broadly accurate and can be relied on for finding things: line ranges, labels and most names check out against the Dutch, and OCR faults are flagged honestly rather than guessed. Two parts misreport Groen's stance: in 7922-8049 the revolutionary premise (state by contract) is given as Groen's own claim, and in 262-393 Groen's critique of Lamartine disappears, leaving only praise. The most frequent minor fault is footnotes from the previous part (whose marks lie before the range) being listed in this part's names and quoted_authors, even where ocr_notes say they belong elsewhere. Covers also tends to drop the long footnotes and Groen's qualifications ('grootendeels', 'nu en dan', 'naar het revolutionair beginsel'), and four covers sentences run past 25 words.
